bounded_statement: Within this submission only: the selected result (two-sided Fisher exact test on 24 coupons, odds ratio 0.0455, p = 0.0094) enters all three coupon rows from each of the 8 print runs into a procedure that treats every row as an independent observation, even though the data description declares print_run_id as the independent-unit column, states the laser setting is fixed for an entire run, and states within-run coupon outcomes are not expected to be independent. With only 8 independent runs (4 per setting), run-level versions of the same comparison (e.g., majority-pass per run: 1/4 nominal vs 4/4 elevated, Fisher p ≈ 0.143) do not reach the reported significance, so the stated conclusion is not supported by the provided workflow and data at the declared unit of independence.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent that the 24 rows span only 8 print runs and lists them, so the run structure is disclosed rather than hidden; however, disclosure does not change the fact that the test statistic and p-value are computed treating the 24 correlated rows as independent observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: run structure disclosed in report but not used in the test

source_refs.quoted_text:
def outcome_counts(rows, setting):
    """Return (passed, failed) coupon counts for one laser-power setting."""
    total = sum(1 for row in rows if row["laser_setting"] == setting)
    passed = sum(
        1
        for row in rows
        if row["laser_setting"] == setting and row["porosity_screen"] == PASS_LABEL
    )
    return passed, total - passed

evidence.description: The report's selected statistical conclusion is based on 24 coupon-level observations and states outright that each coupon row supplies one observation, i.e., 3 repeated entries per authorized independent unit (print run) into the row-independent Fisher procedure.
evidence.observed_value: p = 0.0094 computed from 24 rows drawn from 8 runs

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding three ways. (1) I searched workflow/analysis.py for any aggregation, deduplication, or clustering adjustment keyed on print_run_id (groupby, per-run summaries, cluster-robust or exact run-level tests); none exists — print_run_id is only used to count and list run identifiers in the report text. (2) I checked whether the rows could legitimately be treated as independent despite the run structure; the data description forecloses this by declaring print_run_id the independent unit, stating the laser setting is programmed once per run, and stating within-run outcomes are not expected to be independent. (3) I checked materiality by re-analyzing at the run level: classifying runs by majority outcome gives 1/4 nominal pass-runs vs 4/4 elevated (Fisher exact p ≈ 0.143), and by all-coupons-pass gives 1/4 vs 3/4 (p ≈ 0.486); neither approaches the reported p = 0.0094, so the coupon-level test materially overstates the evidence rather than being a harmless simplification. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py builds the 2x2 Fisher table from per-coupon counts (outcome_counts iterates over all rows and each coupon row supplies one observation) and never aggregates or otherwise adjusts by print_run_id, so the 3 correlated coupons per run are counted as 3 independent trials each, inflating the effective sample size from 8 runs to 24 rows and deflating the p-value.
